title: The turtle without a hard shell
learning_goal: Explain how leatherbacks differ from other sea turtles
subject: marine_biology

approved_facts.statement: The leatherback is the largest living sea turtle.
Unlike other sea turtles, a leatherback lacks a hard bony shell; leathery skin covers connective tissue and overlapping dermal bones.
Seven longitudinal ridges run down the leatherback carapace.
Leatherbacks primarily eat jellyfish and other soft-bodied prey.
Pointed jaws help leatherbacks grasp soft-bodied prey; backward-pointing mouth and throat papillae help retain prey.
